headline: Obernolte leads by 3,687 votes in California's redrawn High Desert seat
dek: Jay Obernolte, a Republican, holds a 1.8-point lead over Tessa Hodge, a first-time Democratic candidate, in a district forecasters rated safely Republican. About 5 percent of the expected vote remains, and AP has not called the race.
summary: In California's 23rd District, Republican Jay Obernolte leads Democrat Tessa Hodge by 1.8 points with the race still uncalled.

paras.text: More than a week after Election Day, Rep. Jay Obernolte, a Republican, leads Tessa Hodge, a Democrat, 106,453 votes to 102,766 in California's 23rd Congressional District. That is a margin of 3,687 votes, or 1.8 points, with 95.18 percent of the expected vote counted. The Associated Press has not called the race. It was not expected to be close. Before the election, the Bay Area Reporter noted that all four of the most watched outfits that rate House races had rated the seat solidly Republican.

Obernolte was seeking a fourth term. Fox News describes him as a computer scientist and video game developer who holds a graduate degree in artificial intelligence. Hodge is 38 and running for office for the first time. She told KVCR, the public station in San Bernardino, that she is a licensed clinical social worker and business owner from Victorville. Her stated priorities were to lower costs, expand healthcare, and create good-paying jobs. Obernolte did not answer KVCR's candidate questionnaire.

The Bay Area Reporter reported that Hodge, who grew up in the Victorville area, quit her full-time job in order to have more time to campaign but kept seeing patients. Before the June primary, Obernolte's campaign sent out mailers attacking Hodge as being too progressive for the district, which raised her profile. Hodge told the paper she took the mailers as a sign that he saw her as the easiest opponent to beat in November. In the general election, she hit Obernolte for holding virtual town halls, saying the format let him screen questions. She also focused on the cost of health care and the region's shortage of medical facilities.

The money was lopsided. According to FEC reports through Oct. 14, as compiled by VoteSee, Obernolte raised $1.9M and Hodge raised $127K. Local reporting has not yet explained why the race tightened so much. The national result is part of the picture: by NBC News projections, Democrats seized control of both the U.S. House and Senate. In California, the Democrat Xavier Becerra won the governor's race over Steve Hilton by 31.3 points, about 11 points better for Democrats than Kamala Harris's 2024 margin in the state.

These were new lines. In 2025, California voters approved Proposition 50, voting to amend their state's constitution so that the new map could be used from 2026 to 2030. The measure was California's response to the Republican redraw in Texas. Ballotpedia's analysis of the plan showed the 23rd becoming slightly more Republican than the commission-drawn version. Hodge told the Bay Area Reporter the change made it even harder for a Democrat to win.

The Antelope Valley Press reports that the district is shared between LA, Kern, Riverside and San Bernardino counties. Its Los Angeles and Kern County pieces include Llano and Valyermo to the south, Lake Los Angeles and California City to the North. Most of the district is the High Desert of San Bernardino County, the area around Victorville and Big Bear. At its southern end it stretches south toward Yucaipa and Calimesa and into the desert communities.

The Watch's data for this seat does not separate the district's share of each of those four counties, so this report cannot say which part of the district moved most. Even a full county breakdown would have a limit. Vote counts cannot show whether a shift came from people changing their minds or from a change in who turned out, and comparable turnout numbers for this district are not available here.

Obernolte has held this seat since 2021, when it was numbered the 8th District. Fox News called the district a High Desert seat in San Bernardino County that was rated Solid R before the midterms. If his lead holds, he will be one of the few California Republicans left in the House. RealClearPolitics counted him among four Republicans on track to make up a state delegation that stood at nine after the 2024 election.

The count is not finished. If AP's estimate of the expected vote is right, about 10,600 ballots remain. Hodge would need roughly two-thirds of them to pull ahead. The California Voter Foundation notes that voters with signature problems have until November 25 to fix them, and the Antelope Valley Press reports that results of Nov. 3 election will be final on Dec. 11. Nationally, AP has called 254 House seats for Democrats and 167 for Republicans. This race is one of 14 still open.
